belongs_to: Figure it out p.158, Q2 'Can you create a similar table for 1/4?' - printed answer table
description:
A boxed table with thin black borders: 2 rows x 4 columns, four columns of roughly equal width. Row 1 is a tall picture row (picture sits in the upper part of each cell, lower part blank); row 2 is a short caption row. Pieces are quarters of a roti drawn as quarter-discs in dusky mauve/maroon: each quarter has a thick maroon curved rim (arc) and, inside it, a right triangle filled with fine horizontal hatch lines whose right angle is at the circle centre; between the triangle's slanted side and the arc is a small white circular segment (lens). Quarters of one cell touch each other and are separated only by thin white cut lines (a horizontal and/or a vertical one).
Column 1: ONE quarter piece only = the top-left quarter of a circle (right angle at its bottom-right corner, arc running from the bottom-left to the top-right). Caption: '1/4 =' (answer blank) and under it '1-time quarter'.
Column 2: TWO quarters stacked = the left half of a disc (flat edge on the right, white horizontal cut line between the upper and lower quarter): top-left quarter + bottom-left quarter. Caption: '1/4 + 1/4 =' (blank) and '2 times quarter'.
Column 3: THREE quarters = a disc with the bottom-right quarter missing: top-left, top-right and bottom-left quarters present, thin white cross lines between them. Caption: '1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 =' (blank) and '3 times quarter'.
Column 4: FOUR quarters = a complete disc cut by a thin white cross (vertical + horizontal line) into 4 equal quarters, each with its hatched triangle pointing at the centre. Caption: '1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 =' (answer blank, the '=' touches the last fraction) and '4 times quarter'.
The right-hand side of every '=' is left empty in the print. Fractions are typeset (numerator over a bar over denominator).
unclear: Exact mauve/maroon colour is approximate (page image is low resolution).
Orientation of the single quarter in column 1 read as right-angle at bottom-right (top-left quarter of a circle); judged from a zoomed crop.

belongs_to: Try Further! Q4a 'Draw a picture and write an addition statement as above to show: a. 5 times 1/4 of a roti' - printed answer picture + addition statement (label 'a.')
description:
Picture of 5 quarters of a roti in a row, in pale pink/lilac with fine horizontal hatch lines and a thin lilac outline (different, lighter style than the table in SOL38-table-2). Left: ONE complete disc made of 4 quarters, separated by a thin white vertical cut line and a thin white horizontal cut line (cross). To its right, with a clear gap, ONE separate fifth quarter: a quarter-disc with its straight vertical edge on the left and its straight flat edge at the bottom (right angle at the bottom-left), arc curving over the top-right; fully hatched, only a very faint outline on the upper left. Total = 4 + 1 = 5 quarters. The label 'a.' stands to the left of the picture.
Under the picture the statement: 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 5/4 = 5 times quarter (five unit fractions 1/4, then '= 5/4 = 5 times quarter').

belongs_to: Try Further! Q4b 'Draw a picture and write an addition statement as above to show: b. 9 times 1/4 of a roti' - printed answer picture + addition statement (label 'b.')
description:
Picture of 9 quarters of a roti in one row, same pale pink/lilac hatched style as SOL38-shape-1. Two COMPLETE discs side by side with a gap (each disc = 4 quarters split by a thin white vertical and a thin white horizontal cut line; the discs are drawn slightly oval, a little taller than wide), then, with a further gap, ONE separate ninth quarter at the right: quarter-disc with the straight vertical edge on the left, flat edge at the bottom, arc over the top-right, hatched, very faint outline on its upper-left. Total = 4 + 4 + 1 = 9 quarters. The label 'b.' stands at the left of the picture (on page 39, continuing Q4 of page 38).
Under the picture: 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 9/4 = 9 times quarter = 2 + 1/4 (nine unit fractions 1/4, counted; the last term 1/4 is a typeset fraction).

belongs_to: Q5 'Match each fractional unit with the correct picture: 1/3, 1/5, 1/8, 1/6' - printed answer (four fraction-arrow-circle rows)
description:
Above the answer, the question's four fractions are reprinted as a bold row (in this order, left to right): 1/3, 1/5, 1/8, 1/6. The answer is 4 rows stacked vertically after the word 'Ans.', in the order 1/3, 1/5, 1/6, 1/8. Each row = the typeset fraction, a blue right-pointing block arrow, then one circle (blue outline, white inside) cut by straight radii from the centre into equal sectors, with EXACTLY ONE sector filled medium blue (darker blue edge on its straight sides):
Row 1: 1/3 -> circle in 3 equal sectors (radii go to the 12 o'clock, 4 o'clock and 8 o'clock positions); the shaded sector is the left/upper-left one, between 8 and 12 o'clock.
Row 2: 1/5 -> circle in 5 equal sectors (radii at 12, about 2:24, 4:48, 7:12 and 9:36 o'clock); the shaded sector is the one just left of 12 o'clock, between about 9:36 and 12.
Row 3: 1/6 -> circle in 6 equal sectors (radii at 12, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 o'clock; one vertical diameter plus two slanted diameters); the shaded sector is between 10 and 12 o'clock.
Row 4: 1/8 -> circle in 8 equal sectors (radii at every 45 degrees: vertical, horizontal and two diagonal diameters); the shaded sector is between 10:30 and 12 o'clock (just left of the top).
The circles are about the same size and lined up in one column to the right of their arrows.
unclear: Sector boundaries read from a zoomed crop; the clock-position of the radii for 1/5 is approximate (equal 72-degree sectors, one edge at 12).
